member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Application
member.summary:
Provides global application state flags and standard engine path roots.
Path semantics mirror Unity's Application API:
- the directory of the running executable (standalone) or project root (editor).
- read-only assets shipped inside the app package. On desktop this is {DataPath}/Content; on Android it maps to the APK's assets/ VFS.
- a writable directory that survives app updates. Per-OS convention (Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%, macOS ~/Library/Application Support, iOS Documents, Linux ~/.local/share).
- a writable scratch directory the OS may evict. Used for transient bundle downloads.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.Lz4Block
member.summary: Describes one compressed block within an LZ4 AssetBundle's data region. The block layout stored on disk is the sequence of these descriptors (each: varint UncompressedOffset, varint UncompressedSize, varint CompressedOffset, varint CompressedSize) immediately before the data region. A reader can locate any uncompressed byte offset by scanning the block table and decompress only the single covering block.

member.summary: Static helpers for compressing/decompressing AssetBundle payloads with LZ4.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompression.DefaultBlockSize
member.summary: Default uncompressed block size. Smaller blocks mean finer seek granularity and less decompression wasted on partial reads; larger blocks mean better ratio. 1 MiB matches Unity's chunk-based LZ4 default and is a good balance for typical assets.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompression.CompressBound(System.Int32)
member.summary: Maximum bound for the compressed form of bytes.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompression.Compress(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Compress a single block. Always returns valid LZ4-encoded bytes (LZ4 can store incompressible input as literal runs, so the output is always decodable). The result may be slightly larger than the input for tiny/incompressible data; callers that want size gains should compare modes at the bundle level, not the block level.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompression.Decompress(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte},System.Span{System.Byte})
member.summary: Decompress a block into a caller-provided buffer of exactly the uncompressed size.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompression.CompressStream(System.IO.Stream,System.IO.Stream,System.Int32)
member.summary: Compress a full stream into using fixed-size uncompressed blocks, returning the block table (offsets are relative to the start of the data region). The caller is responsible for writing the block table header before this output's bytes. For mode=None, this is not used - the data is copied verbatim.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompressionMode
member.summary: Compression algorithm stored in an AssetBundle's container header. The header records this byte so the reader knows how to decompress the data region. is the default for new bundles; is used for bundles that must stream without decompression cost (e.g. very large scene bundles) and is the fallback when LZ4 encoding fails.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompressionMode.None
member.summary: No compression. Payload bytes are stored verbatim. Fastest load, largest disk size.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.AssetBundles.BundleCompressionMode.Lz4Block
member.summary: LZ4 block compression (via K4os.Compression.LZ4). Decompression is extremely fast and the container stores a block table so individual blocks can be decompressed on demand for streaming. This is the default for new bundles.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetImporting.LightmapUVGenerator
member.summary:
Generates a second UV set (UV2) suitable for lightmapping by running XEngine.Unwrapper over a mesh and baking the resulting atlas UVs into .
The unwrapper produces per-corner UVs (one per triangle corner) with seams between charts, whereas a Mesh stores per-vertex attributes. So we split vertices wherever corners that share an original vertex disagree on their lightmap UV, duplicating every other attribute (position, normal, uv, tangent, color, bone data) onto the new vertices. The index buffer keeps the same length and triangle order, so existing submesh ranges stay valid.

member.summary: Unwrap and write the result into its UV2 channel. Best-effort: on failure (degenerate geometry, etc.) it logs a warning and leaves the mesh unchanged.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetImporting.IModelTextureResolver
member.summary:
Strategy for turning a model's texture references into s during import. Invoked once per distinct texture the model references (the caller caches and reuses the result across every material slot that references the same texture).
The default (used when nothing else is supplied) decodes and GPU-uploads immediately - correct for a direct runtime load with no separate asset-tracking step to hand off to. The editor supplies its own implementation that never decodes another asset's pixel data itself: an externally referenced texture is resolved purely by path, against the asset database's existing GUID for that file, and an embedded texture is registered as a proper sub-asset for the asset database to own and cache - so importing a model never grows or duplicates the pixel data of anything else.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetLoader
member.summary:
Deserializes assets off the main/render thread on desktop (one dedicated background thread), so a scene can appear immediately while its meshes/textures stream in.
On WASM there is no worker thread (WasmEnableThreads=false). Requests stay in the same queues and drains them with a per-frame time budget. Blocking wait on the rAF thread is forbidden.
Requests are de-duplicated and split into a High-priority queue (blocking calls) drained before the Normal queue (fire-and-forget resolves).
The actual deserialize runs via . GPU resources created during load are safe because Graphics.Submit is thread-safe and the render thread drains continuously on desktop.

member.summary: Queue a non-blocking background load. No-op if already cached/queued/in-flight.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.AssetLoader.LoadBlocking(System.Guid)
member.summary: Load with priority and block until it finishes, returning the instance (or null if it couldn't be loaded). Used by . On WASM this loads inline on the calling (rAF) thread — a Wait would freeze the frame.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.AssetLoader.Tick(System.Int32)
member.summary: Drain queued loads. Desktop: no-op (the background thread owns the queue). WASM: process high then normal until the millisecond budget is exhausted, then return to rAF.

member.summary: Stop the loader thread (desktop) and release any blocked callers. Called at shutdown.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetLoadingConfig
member.summary:
Global toggle for asynchronous (background-threaded) asset loading.
When is true, resolves non-blocking: it returns the cached instance if present, otherwise queues a load on the background thread and returns null until the asset streams in. When false, .Res blocks and loads synchronously (legacy behavior).
Driven by the "Async Asset Loading" project setting (default ON). The editor's settings apply path and the standalone PlayerSettingsLoader both write here.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.AssetRef`1
member.summary: A serializable reference to an asset. Stores a GUID for persistent identification and caches the resolved instance. When the asset is needed, it's loaded via AssetDatabase.Get(). This solves the "stale reference" problem all references to the same asset share the same resolved instance, and re-resolving always gets the latest version.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.AssetRef`1.Res
member.summary:
The resolved asset.
When async asset loading is enabled (), this is non-blocking: it returns the cached instance if available, otherwise it queues a background load and returns null for now. Callers MUST handle a transient null (the asset will stream in over subsequent frames). Use when an immediate value is required. When async loading is disabled, this blocks and loads synchronously (legacy behavior).
Also returns null if the asset is genuinely missing or this ref is explicitly null.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.AssetRef`1.ResWeak
member.summary: Returns the cached instance without attempting to load. May be null.

member.summary:
Render this light's shadow map(s) into the shared shadow atlas.
Implementations rent and submit their own per face (point lights), cascade (directional), or single tile (spot). They CANNOT share a CB across multiple faces because each face calls which uploads view/proj into the single GlobalUniforms UBO sharing a CB would queue all the face draws to execute against whatever matrices the LAST face uploaded.
The shadow atlas itself has already been bound + cleared by the caller in a separate setup CB before this method runs.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.ParticleSystem.Modules.LightModule
member.summary:
When enabled, every alive particle emits a point light into the scene. Lights register with the dynamic SceneLightSystem BVH and so contribute to the same forward-lit surfaces all other lights do, including BRDF, fog scattering, etc. Particles never cast shadows (they'd swamp the closest-N atlas budget instantly).
Cost: each frame the particle proxies refit the dynamic BVH. For 1000 particles that's ~one tree rebuild per frame, low microseconds. Don't enable this on million-particle debris systems unless you've measured it.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Collider.SharedMaterial
member.summary: Friction and bounciness for this collider's surface, or null to inherit.
member.remarks:
With no material the collider falls back to the project's default material, and failing that to its 's own friction and restitution. That layering is what lets a body set one surface for all its colliders and have an individual collider override it — a metal crate with one rubber face.
Assigning while the collider is already touching something takes effect on the existing contacts rather than waiting for them to separate; see World.RefreshMaterial.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Collider.SweepVelocityThreshold
member.summary: Relative approach speed above which a pair involving this collider gets a swept test, or 0 to use the world's .
member.remarks: Only consulted when the rigidbody's asks for sweeping at all. Set this on the collider that is easy to tunnel through — a thin wall, a floorboard — rather than lowering the world value, which would make every other pair in the scene pay for sweeps it does not need. A pair uses the lower of the two colliders' thresholds.

member.summary: Builds an inertia tensor for a body whose shapes have no usable volume (e.g. concave TriangleShapes). member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Rigidbody3D.AddForce(XEngine.Vector.Float3,XEngine.Runtime.ForceMode)
member.summary: Applies a linear effect to the body, interpreted according to .
member.remarks: The instant modes change velocity here and now and wake the body; the continuous modes queue into the force accumulator, which the simulation turns into a velocity delta at the end of one step and integrates during the next — so a queued force shows up in two steps after the call, not one. That is the kernel's pipelining, and gravity arrives the same way. Ignored for non-dynamic bodies, which the simulation moves rather than pushes.

member.summary: Applies an angular effect to the body, interpreted according to .
member.remarks: The angular counterpart of , with the inertia tensor playing the part mass plays there. The mass-independent modes therefore need the tensor itself rather than its inverse, and give up if it cannot be inverted — which is the case for a body whose rotation is fully locked by .

member.summary: Converts a rotation for the simulation, normalising it on the way.
member.remarks: The kernel asserts that an assigned orientation is a unit quaternion, and only in Debug builds — so a rotation that drifted off unit length by composing many small rotations throws in the editor and silently skews inertia in a shipped player. member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.TriggerVolume
member.summary:
A non-solid sensor volume. It does not collide with or push anything; instead it queries the physics world each fixed step for overlapping rigidbodies and raises enter/stay/exit events. Use it for pickups, checkpoints, damage zones, detectors, and similar gameplay triggers.
Only bodies that can be identified (a ) are reported. Static geometry shares a per-layer body and has no component to hand back, so it is ignored.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.WheelCollider
member.summary:
A raycast-vehicle wheel. Ground contact is a grid of downward rays across the wheel face, riding over bumps/kerbs; the ray distances are analytic so the contact is stable. Suspension is a spring/damper tuned from a natural frequency, grip uses a saturating slip model clamped to a friction circle, and a fully compressed wheel depenetrates out of the surface.
The wheel applies forces to the parent ; it does not add a collision shape of its own. Place the wheel GameObject so its position marks the top of the suspension travel; the wheel hangs below along -up.

member.summary: Drives GameObject-UI input, Unity-style. A scene needs exactly one enabled for its es to receive pointer and keyboard events. member.remarks: This is entirely game-space: it ticks from (play mode only) and nothing in the engine loop drives it. A has no dependency on it - delete this component and canvases still render, they just stop receiving input - so you can drop in your own event system. Access the active one through .

member.summary: Owns the Scribe and its glyph atlas for the retained-mode UI framework. There is one instance per process - UI text from every shares it (matching how most engines treat font atlases).
member.remarks:
Implements .
The retained-mode pipeline does NOT call ; instead, walks and emits per-glyph quads via , sampling the atlas texture in the fragment shader.
Atlas growth: when Scribe runs out of room it allocates a new (larger) texture via . The previous texture is released by Scribe; consumers must re-read every frame and not cache the reference past a possible re-allocation. .AtlasVersion increments on any mutation (new glyph or grow), giving consumers a cheap way to detect staleness.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Game.PreparePaperFrame
member.summary:
Called each frame right before Paper.BeginFrame. Sets Paper's logical resolution to the window's logical size (OS points) and DisplayFramebufferScale to . Quill's TransformPoint multiplies every vertex by DisplayFramebufferScale, so vertices span [0, winSize × cs] = [0, fbSize], exactly matching the orthographic projection set up by .
A widget declared Width(100) occupies 100 logical points = 100 physical pixels at 1× DPI and 200 physical pixels at 2× (Retina) DPI the same physical size on screen regardless of display density, with higher pixel quality on HiDPI displays.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.GameObject.BackPatchTrappedDefinitions(XEngine.Echo.EchoObject,XEngine.Echo.SerializationContext)
member.summary: Phase-2 recovery for objects whose definition was serialized inline inside a missing component. Runs after the whole graph is deserialized (via ), so every reference placeholder already exists with its correct type. Walks the trapped data and, for any node that carries a body, populates the matching placeholder in place (so a $type-less object such as a GameObject - whose type came from the now-missing declared field - is still recovered), or materializes a self-describing definition that nothing else referenced. Best-effort; failures are swallowed.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.MonoBehaviour.ShouldTickGameplay
member.summary: Whether this component's per-frame ticks (Update/LateUpdate/FixedUpdate) should run. Like but additionally frozen while play mode is paused (the editor Step button releases exactly one frame). [ExecuteAlways] components keep ticking — they drive edit-mode previews and must not depend on play state. Lifecycle callbacks (Start/OnEnable/OnDisable) intentionally stay un-gated by pause so objects activated while paused still initialize.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.SceneComponentRegistry
member.summary: Per-scene registry of the components that actually implement a per-frame callback (Start/Update/LateUpdate/FixedUpdate, plus OnRenderCollect/DrawGizmos/OnGui). Components register when they become enabled in an active scene and unregister when disabled/removed, so each loop iterates a short, pre-filtered, execution-ordered list instead of walking every GameObject and component. This is why stores its components in insertion order - ordering for callbacks is owned here, decoupled from component storage.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.SceneComponentRegistry.ClearTypeTickCache
member.summary: Clears the static type-tick cache. Called during hot-reload so user-script MonoBehaviour Types (registered when preview scenes instantiate model/prefab hierarchies) don't pin the collectible script AssemblyLoadContext.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.SceneComponentRegistry.GetPhysicsCallbacks(XEngine.Runtime.MonoBehaviour)
member.summary: Which physics callbacks a component implements. Cached per type, so this costs a dictionary lookup rather than reflection after the first call.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.SceneComponentRegistry.Channel
member.summary: One callback's membership: an insertion-ordered list plus an execution-order-sorted snapshot rebuilt only when membership changes. Iterating the snapshot also keeps a loop safe against components enabling/disabling others mid-callback.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.CommandOpcode
member.summary:
Identifies every kind of command that can be recorded into a .
The executor switches on this value to decide how to decode the payload that follows the header. Adding a new opcode requires: 1. An entry here. 2. A writer method on . 3. A case in the active backend command translator.
Numbering is stable for the lifetime of the process; the wire format is in-memory only, so changing values doesn't break anything as long as encoder and executor agree.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.PropertyStatePool
member.summary:
Pool for the snapshots that rents when it needs to capture a material's properties at encode time. Without this pool, every cmd.Blit call inside an image effect would allocate a fresh (12 dictionaries) just to defend against mid-encoding material mutation.
Buffers track their own rentals and return them in so the pool's lifetime is bounded by the CommandBuffer pool's lifetime.

member.summary: Rent a fresh PropertyState, pre-populated with a copy of 's entries. Caller owns until .

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.TransientStore
member.summary:
A per-CommandBuffer bump-pointer arena for "blob" payloads (matrix arrays, buffer uploads, texture pixel data, debug labels). The encoder copies caller data into the store so the user's source span/array can go away immediately; the executor reads back out by offset+length.
Backing storage is rented from . On reset the store keeps one page and returns the rest to the pool, so a steady-state buffer doesn't churn GC at all.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.RHI.GraphicsPipelineKey
member.summary:
Exact backend pipeline-cache key. Keeps the full raster state instead of relying on a hash-only lookup, so collisions cannot select an incompatible PSO.
When the caller supplies the vertex declaration(s), identity is the interned s rather than the vertex-array handle — every mesh with an identical declaration then shares one PSO per shader/raster/topology instead of compiling its own. stays on the struct purely as the carrier the backend uses to build vertex-input state on a cache miss (PSOs bind vertex buffers at draw time, so any same-layout VAO produces an interchangeable pipeline). Without formats the handle remains part of identity (legacy per-VAO behavior).

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.RHI.GraphicsPipelineKey.SampleCount
member.summary: Multisample count of the render targets this PSO rasterizes into. A pipeline compiled for 1× cannot be bound while a 4× target is set, so this must be part of identity — otherwise the first PSO cached for a shader/raster combination would be reused for both and the driver would reject (or silently mis-rasterize) the mismatched draw.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.RHI.RenderThreadGraphicsDevice
member.summary:
Backend-neutral render-thread decorator. Wraps an whose translates and submits synchronously on the caller's thread (D3D12, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU) and moves that work onto one dedicated thread, so the main thread only pays for encoding the byte-stream .
Ordering: every device operation is marshalled through a single FIFO queue, so the inner device observes exactly the call order it would have seen on a single thread. Frame lifecycle, transient-arena resets and descriptor-pool recycling therefore keep working unchanged; nothing inside the backend needs to know a render thread exists.
Blocking: calls with a return value (BeginFrame(surface), Resize, WaitIdle, surface create/destroy) and Execute(wait: true) block until the render thread reaches that job. BeginFrame() and fire-and-forget Execute do not block — that is where the overlap comes from.
OpenGL is never wrapped: it owns its own render thread because the GL context has hard thread affinity.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.RHI.RenderThreadGraphicsDevice.MaxQueuedFrames
member.summary: How many presented frames the main thread may run ahead of the render thread. 0 (default) keeps the historical behaviour: blocks until this frame has been submitted and presented. 1 enables stage-B pipelining: blocks on the previous frame instead, handing the vsync wait to the render thread and giving the main thread a full frame of budget. Values above 1 are clamped to 1 (deeper queues only add input latency and unbounded memory). Must only be changed from the thread that drives the frame loop.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.RHI.Shaders.DxcShaderCompiler.CanCompileSpirv
member.summary: Probes whether the resolved DXC can emit SPIR-V (needed for the Vulkan backend). Runs a trivial HLSL compile with -spirv and caches the result so callers only pay the process spawn once. Hosts call this before committing to Vulkan so a Windows-SDK-only machine (DXC without -DENABLE_SPIRV_CODEGEN) can fall back to D3D12 / OpenGL instead of crashing on the first shader.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.VertexFormat.LayoutId
member.summary: Interned identity of this vertex declaration's CONTENT (semantics, types, counts, offsets, strides, divisors, normalization, total size). Two formats describing the same layout share one id, so pipeline-state caches can key on the declaration instead of the vertex-array object — identical-layout meshes then share PSOs. Interning uses exact content equality (no hashing shortcuts), so distinct layouts can never collide.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.VertexFormat.VertexLayoutRegistry
member.summary: Exact-content interning registry backing .

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.VertexFormat.VertexType
member.summary:
Component type for a vertex attribute.
Numeric values match OpenGL GL_BYTE / GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE / GL_SHORT / GL_INT / GL_FLOAT so the OpenGL path can pass them through raw. The stride logic in constructors also depends on these thresholds (5121 / 5122).
Other backends must not treat these as native API enums — map via a VertexTypeMapper table (OpenGL: identity; Vulkan/D3D12: to VkFormat / DXGI_FORMAT). Do not renumber these values without updating Size calculation and any serialized mesh data.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Jobs.JobBatch
member.summary: One unit of scheduled work. Batches are pooled, so every access from a worker has to prove it is still looking at the generation it was handed. packs the generation and the chunk cursor into one 64-bit interlocked word precisely so that proof and the claim happen in a single atomic step: a worker that wakes up late on a recycled batch fails the version check inside the CAS and leaves without touching anything.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.Jobs.JobBatch.Claim
member.summary: High 32 bits = generation, low 32 bits = next unclaimed chunk index.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Jobs.JobSystem
member.summary:
Minimal data-parallel job system: a reusable worker pool, a chunked parallel-for, dependency handles, and a main-thread Complete() that helps drain instead of idling.
Deliberately not a general task scheduler. There is one global FIFO of batches, workers claim chunks out of a batch with an interlocked cursor, and the thread that calls joins in. That keeps the whole thing small enough to reason about for the render-loop consumers it exists for (frustum culling, skinning matrices, animation graph evaluation), all of which are "split a flat index range, write disjoint slots" shaped.
(or XENGINE_JOBS=0) forces every schedule to run inline on the caller: same results, no threads. That makes "is this a parallelism bug?" a one-flag experiment and gives the parity tests a serial reference to compare against.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Jobs.JobSystem.Enabled
member.summary: Master switch. Defaults to on when the machine has more than one core, unless XENGINE_JOBS=0 is set. Turning it off makes every schedule run inline on the calling thread.

The body must only touch state private to its own range; the render-loop consumers all write disjoint array slots, which is race-free in the CLR object model even for bool[] (byte-granular writes never disturb neighbours).

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.CollisionDetectionMode
member.summary: How hard a works to avoid passing through obstacles within one step.
member.remarks: A body moving faster than its own thickness per step can start a step on one side of a wall and end it on the other, with no overlap at either sample point for the solver to react to. The continuous modes close that gap with a swept test that finds where the two shapes first touch and places a contact there. Values match Unity's CollisionDetectionMode.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.CollisionDetectionMode.Discrete
member.summary: No swept test; contacts appear only once shapes overlap.
member.remarks: The default, and enough for anything that does not move a large fraction of its own size per step.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.CollisionDetectionMode.Continuous
member.summary: Swept against static and kinematic colliders; discrete against other rigidbodies.
member.remarks: The usual choice for a projectile: level geometry is what it must not escape through, and leaving dynamic partners discrete keeps the cost down.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.CollisionDetectionMode.ContinuousDynamic
member.summary: Swept against static and kinematic colliders, and against rigidbodies that are themselves or .
member.remarks: Both sides have to opt in, so a fast body among many discrete objects still sweeps against none of them.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.CollisionDetectionMode.ContinuousSpeculative
member.summary: Swept against every partner, unconditionally.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.ContactEventDispatcher
member.summary: Turns the physics step's overlap and contact state into Unity-style OnTrigger* and OnCollision* callbacks. Runs once per step, on the main thread, after has finished.
member.remarks: Trigger transitions come straight from the kernel, which tracks sensor overlaps natively (see ThirdParty/Jitter2/PATCHES.md). Collisions are tracked here instead, because "touching" is finer-grained than an arbiter's lifetime: an arbiter can exist with no live contact slots while the shapes sit within the speculative margin, which is not a collision as far as gameplay is concerned. The freshness bookkeeping mirrors the kernel's, so both event kinds behave the same around sleep.

member.remarks: A contact only bounces once its approach speed exceeds , which is what stops a bouncy body from jittering forever instead of coming to rest.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.BakeMesh(XEngine.Runtime.Resources.Mesh)
member.summary:
Bake (or fetch the cached) physics representation of a mesh. The bake is stored directly on the instance (), so its lifetime is tied to the mesh rather than a separate global cache. The result is shared by every collider that uses the mesh, so the bake happens once instead of per MeshCollider instance, and is rebuilt automatically when the mesh's changes.
Thread-safe. The bake is pure CPU work, so this may be called from worker threads to pre-bake meshes off the main thread (independent meshes bake in parallel; each mesh locks on itself).

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.ContactEvents
member.summary: Turns the step's overlap and contact state into OnTrigger* / OnCollision* callbacks.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld._staticRigidbodiesByLayer
member.summary: Static rigidbodies indexed by layer. Each layer has its own static rigidbody to ensure collision filtering works correctly. Orphan colliders (colliders without a Rigidbody3D component) will attach to the static rigidbody for their layer.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld._compositeBroadPhaseFilter
member.summary: Composite filter that chains multiple broad phase filters together.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.AutoSyncTransforms
member.summary: Whether Transform edits are pushed into the physics system immediately (before physics queries), or only batched right before the FixedUpdate step. Matches Unity's Physics.autoSyncTransforms: when true, a query right after moving a Transform sees the new pose; when false, call manually (the pre-step sync still happens every FixedUpdate either way). This only concerns the transform -> body direction; the body -> transform readback after a step is separate and always runs for dynamic/kinematic bodies.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.SyncTransforms
member.summary: Pushes any changed Transforms into their physics bodies (transform -> body). Runs automatically before each simulation step and, when is on, before queries. Call it manually to make Transform edits visible to queries when auto-sync is off. Only bodies whose Transform actually changed since the last sync are updated, so it is cheap when idle.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.EnhancedDeterminism
member.summary: When true, uses Jitter2's deterministic island-based solver instead of the regular parallel solver. Slower but produces identical results across runs required for networked physics, replays, or lockstep simulation.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.ThreadModel
member.summary: Thread model for the physics step. Persistent keeps worker threads alive between steps (lower latency, higher idle CPU). Regular spins them up per step (higher latency, lower idle CPU).

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.EnableAuxiliaryContactPoints
member.summary: Generates extra contact points along the perimeter of contact patches for improved stability on flat surfaces. Default true. Disable for slight perf gain at the cost of stability.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.PersistentContactManifold
member.summary: Persists contact manifolds across frames (warm-starts the solver). Default true. Disable for slight memory savings; significantly hurts stack stability if turned off.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.SpeculativeRelaxationFactor
member.summary: Damping factor (0..1) applied to speculative contact correction. Lower = softer prediction. Default 0.9.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.SweepVelocityThreshold
member.summary: Relative approach speed above which a continuous pair gets a swept test. Default 10.
member.remarks: The speed that risks tunnelling is roughly the thinner shape's thickness divided by the fixed timestep, so this world-wide value has to suit the thinnest geometry in the scene. Rather than lowering it and making every pair pay, set on the geometry that needs it.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.BounceThreshold
member.summary: Approach speed a contact must exceed before bounciness is applied at all. Matches Unity's Physics.bounceThreshold. Default 1.
member.remarks: A resting contact still reports a small approach velocity every step; bouncing on it would mean a bouncy body never settles. Raise this to suppress small bounces, lower it to let light taps bounce. Applies to contact pairs formed after the change, not to ones already being solved.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.DefaultMaterial
member.summary: The material used by colliders with no of their own. Matches Unity's Physics.defaultPhysicsMaterial.
member.remarks: Null by default, in which case a collider without a material falls back to the friction and restitution of its own — the behaviour before materials existed.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.PhysicsWorld.QueriesHitTriggers
member.summary: Whether queries report trigger colliders. Matches Unity's Physics.queriesHitTriggers. Default true.
member.remarks: Applies to raycasts, shape casts and overlap tests unless a call passes other than .

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.RigidbodyConstraints
member.summary: World-space degrees of freedom a is not allowed to move along.
member.remarks: The bit values match Unity's RigidbodyConstraints, including its unused low bit, so that authored values and inspector bitmasks carry over unchanged.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.RigidbodyInterpolation
member.summary: How a smooths its Transform between fixed physics steps.
member.remarks: Physics advances at while frames are presented at whatever rate the display runs at. Without smoothing, a body's Transform holds still for the frames between two steps and then jumps, which reads as stutter at any refresh rate that is not an exact multiple of the fixed rate. Values match Unity's RigidbodyInterpolation.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.RigidbodyInterpolation.None
member.summary: The Transform is the simulated pose, updated only when a step happens.
member.remarks: The default, and the right choice for a body nothing watches closely — no per-body state, and the Transform and the simulation never disagree.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.RigidbodyInterpolation.Interpolate
member.summary: The Transform is interpolated between the two most recent simulated poses.
member.remarks: Smooth and never overshoots, at the cost of the Transform trailing the simulation by up to one fixed step. The usual choice for anything the player follows, a camera target above all.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.RigidbodyInterpolation.Extrapolate
member.summary: The Transform is extrapolated forward from the latest simulated pose using current velocity.
member.remarks: No lag, but it predicts through collisions it cannot know about, so a body reaching a wall visibly penetrates it and then snaps back. Prefer unless the lag itself is the problem.

member.summary: The minimum Vulkan capability envelope a HarmonyOS device must meet before the player is allowed to render. member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.ClusterLightList
member.summary:
Per-camera clustered light list (P3.2): replaces the per-fragment dual-BVH walk in the Standard forward/deferred lighting path with a single cluster lookup + compact light index loop (URP Forward+ style).
The screen is divided into a fixed x grid in normalized NDC space (resolution / SSAA independent) crossed with exponential view-depth slices. Per frame and per camera the CPU rasterizes every active local light's bounding sphere into the grid conservatively (world AABB corners through the camera view-projection; any corner behind the eye falls back to full-screen coverage) and builds one compact index list per cluster.
GPU layout (single RGBA32F square power-of-two texture, texelFetch only):
texel c in [0, ClusterCount) : header for cluster c .x = floatBits(firstEntrySlot) absolute entry slot (texel*4+channel) .y = floatBits(entryCount) entry slot s (s >= ClusterCount*4): texel s>>2, channel s&3 floatBits(encoded) encoded = slot+1 for the static BVH, -(slot+1) for the dynamic BVH
Cluster linear index = (slice * TilesY + tileY) * TilesX + tileX, matching the shader.
Correctness contract: the per-cluster list is a conservative superset of the BVH result for every world position inside that cluster. Lights outside their range contribute exactly zero radiance (the attenuation window is zero at d >= range), so evaluating the superset yields the same lighting as the BVH walk.

member.summary: Always 1. MSAA used to be faked with a 2× internal scale (2× SSAA = 4× pixel-shading cost) that a downsampling blit resolved. The RHI now has real multisample render targets, so the camera renders at native resolution into a multisample target and resolves it — the sample buffers scale with the sample count, the shading cost does not. Kept as a method so callers and tests that asked for the stand-in scale keep compiling and observe the removal.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.DefaultRenderPipeline.GetEffectiveMsaaSampleCount(XEngine.Runtime.CameraClearFlags,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Sample count actually used for this camera's color target, after clamping to what the device supports and excluding the configurations whose single-sample interop the RHI cannot serve. Returns 1 when MSAA is off or unusable, in which case the pipeline renders exactly as it did before.
MSAA is skipped when: the device reports no support for the requested count; the renderer is 2D or Deferred (both blit single-sample depth into the camera color target, which no API allows against a multisample attachment, and deferred MSAA additionally needs per-sample lighting); the clear flags are Depth/Nothing (they blit the previous camera's single-sample color in); the frame needs the editor depth copy (grid/gizmos without a prepass blit depth out of the camera target, equally illegal while multisampled); or an after-opaques image effect is active (SSAO/SSR/SSGI and friends sample SceneColor while the camera target is still the multisample one — the resolve only happens after transparents, so there is no single-sample copy for them to read).

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.GiProbeVolume
member.summary: Dynamic irradiance probe volume (Surface Cache GI, probe tier): a camera-following snapped grid of probes whose octahedral irradiance tiles live in a persistent RGBA16F atlas. A round-robin batch of tiles is refreshed per frame by the SSGI shader's ProbeUpdate pass (screen-space rays over the current frame's radiance, alpha-blended EMA), and lit shaders sample the volume via _GIMode 3 / SampleGiProbes. Grid params reach shaders through a 2-texel RGBA32F data texture so no backend cbuffer ABI changes are needed. v1: single volume owned by the last camera that prepared it (primary camera scenarios); a world-space surface cache is the v2 upgrade path.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.GiProbeVolume.Bind(XEngine.Runtime.CommandBuffer)
member.summary: Binds the atlas + grid data texture as shader globals (before opaque draws). Strict backends (D3D12/Vulkan) require every reflected texture slot to be bound, so the inactive path pins dummies (ScreenSpaceShadows.BindDisabled convention): the black data texture's alpha also makes GiProbesActive() read false in-shader.

member.summary: Subpixel Morphological Anti-Aliasing (SMAA 1x) with luma edge detection. A spatial post-process alternative to with cleaner edges and no temporal ghosting. Runs on LDR/perceptual color, so place it late in (after tonemapping), like FXAA. Don't stack it with FXAA or TAA.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.TAAEffect
member.summary:
Temporal Anti-Aliasing image effect. Jitters the camera projection matrix each frame using a Halton sequence and accumulates samples over time, using motion vectors to reproject the previous frame's result.
Usage: 1. Add TAAEffect to Camera.Effects. 2. Motion vectors are always produced by the unified prepass. 3. OnPreCull applies the sub-pixel jitter to the camera's ProjectionMatrix while NonJitteredProjectionMatrix stays clean. 4. OnRenderEffect resolves the jittered frame against the reprojected history.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.LightBVH
member.summary:
Bounding-volume hierarchy of localized lights (point + spot) for forward rendering.
One instance is owned by each : a "static" tree for lights flagged non-moving and a "dynamic" tree for everything else. Per fragment the shader walks both trees stacklessly via rope links to find lights whose tight AABB contains the fragment position, then accumulates their contributions.
Light slots are stable identifiers in [0, capacity). They survive topology changes so the per-light data texture rarely needs to be re-uploaded. Topology changes (add / remove / "moved past loose buffer") rebuild the tree top-down with a median split. Lights whose new tight AABB still fits inside the previously-stored loose AABB only refit a single leaf node no parent updates needed because internal node bounds were derived from the loose bounds.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.LightBVH.DefaultLooseFactor
member.summary: How much each light's tight AABB is inflated to produce its loose AABB. 0.25 means the light can drift 25 % of its range past its tight bounds before reinsertion.

member.summary: One float4 of light data uploaded per slot. Must match LightBVH.glsl.

member.summary: Two float4 per node (min/hit, max/miss). Must match LightBVH.glsl.

member.summary: Per-slot light parameters. Updated by / .

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.LightBVH.Node
member.summary:
Stackless rope BVH node. Layout matches the GPU exactly (2 float4): (Min.xyz, Hit) / (Max.xyz, Miss).
Internal: Hit = first child index, Miss = escape index. Leaf: Hit = encoded slot ( -(slot+1) ), Miss = escape index. Escape index of -1 = "traversal complete".

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.LightProbeVolume
member.summary: Runtime light-probe sampler. Built from a baked set of probe positions + SH and a precomputed tetrahedralization (tetra vertex indices + per-face neighbour links, produced by the editor's bake). locates the tetrahedron containing a world position, then barycentric-blends the four corner probes' SH; points outside the hull fall back to a nearby blend.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.LightProbeVolume.ComputeBarycentric(System.Int32,XEngine.Vector.Float3,System.Single@,System.Single@,System.Single@,System.Single@)
member.summary: Barycentric coords of in tetra (b0 = corner 0, etc.). Returns false only when the tetrahedron is degenerate (near-zero volume) - the grid tetrahedralization can emit zero-volume slivers on the real positions - so the caller skips it. The coordinates are output even when is outside the tet (some negative), so the caller can both test containment and find the nearest boundary tet for extrapolation.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.RenderPipeline.RenderBatch
member.summary: Represents a render batch: a group of objects sharing the same material, mesh, and shader pass. Batching reduces GPU state changes by binding material uniforms once for all objects in the batch.

Renders all given objects with optimized batching. Objects are grouped by (material, mesh, pass) to minimize GPU state changes. This achieves: - Material uniforms bound once per batch (instead of per object) - Mesh data uploaded once per batch - Shader variant selected once per batch - Per-object uniforms still bound individually
Performance: 100 objects with same material = 1 material bind (vs 100 without batching)
member.param: CommandBuffer the batches encode into. The caller is responsible for binding the target framebuffer + viewport before calling this method, and for submitting the buffer after.
Currently bound color render target, used for the GrabTexture handshake (read FB for the blit-into-grab-RT). Pass null if no pass in this batch will request a grab texture.
When true, skip shaders that already wrote a GBuffer pass (Deferred hybrid: Lit deferred, Unlit/Terrain stay Forward).

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SceneLightSystem
member.summary:
Per-scene owner of the static and dynamic light BVHs and their GPU-side mirrors. The render pipeline calls once per frame with the lights collected from the scene; this class adds / removes / refits as needed and uploads only the dirty rows of each texture.
One directional light is treated specially: it never enters either BVH and is uploaded via the existing cascade-shadow uniform path on the render pipeline.
A bounded number of point + spot lights win shadow atlas slots each frame, picked by camera distance. Lights that miss the cut still light surfaces; they just sample as unshadowed.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SceneLightSystem.MaxShadowCasters
member.summary: How many local lights (point + spot combined) can have shadow atlas slots in a single frame. Bump (C# + ShaderLibrary) together.

member.name: F:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SceneLightSystem.ClusteredLightingEnabled
member.summary:
Master switch for the clustered light-list path (P3.2). When false (or when a camera's cluster build is skipped) the shaders fall back to the per-fragment BVH walk via the runtime enabled flag in _ClusterGridParams.w.
Defaults to false: measured on Vulkan the clustered path is a wash-to-slightly-worse against the existing rope-BVH once the per-camera CPU build (0.35-1.7 ms depending on light count) is counted, so enabling it by default would be a small net regression. See docs/benchmarks/2026-08-19-p32-clustered-light-lists/ for the A/B data and the analysis of why (XEngine's BVH already does tight sphere leaf tests with early-out traversal, unlike the naive per-light loop that Forward+ clustering normally replaces). The path is kept, verified pixel-identical, and flag-switchable so a future GPU-side (compute shader) cluster build can be dropped in without redoing the shader work.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SceneLightSystem.Directional
member.summary: The directional light selected this frame, or null. Render pipeline takes this for cascade shadows + the directional uniform slot.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SceneLightSystem.ShadowCasters
member.summary: Lights that won shadow atlas slots this frame, in order. The pipeline calls RenderShadows on each.

member.summary: True when this frame needs a shadow atlas clear + shadow pass (directional with shadows and/or any selected local shadow casters). Empty scenes skip the 4K/8K depth clear.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SceneLightSystem.Reconcile(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.IRenderableLight},XEngine.Vector.Float3,XEngine.Runtime.LayerMask)
member.summary:
Walk this frame's lights, register / unregister with the appropriate BVH, refit dynamics, pick the directional + closest-N shadow casters, and upload only the dirty rows of each texture. Cheap when nothing changed.
Note on : per-camera light filtering by GameObject layer is not applied here. The BVH is a per-scene structure. Lighting membership uses the separate 8-bit packed into each leaf (shader AND with the object's mask). Camera still culls renderers, not lights.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Rendering.SMAALookupTextures
member.summary:
Loads the two precomputed SMAA lookup textures (AreaTex and SearchTex) from embedded resources, caching one shared GPU texture each.
Both are stored as raw RGBA8 (the reference RG8/R8 data expanded into the R/G channels: AreaTex = [R,G,0,255], SearchTex = [R,0,0,255]) in the upstream row order. The reference data comes from https://github.com/iryoku/smaa (Textures/AreaTex.h, Textures/SearchTex.h), MIT licensed.
Note: unlike turol/smaaDemo's raw-GL path (which vertically flips these textures under RENDERER_OPENGL via flipSMAATextures), XEngine must NOT flip them - its blit / render-target sampling already presents them in the upstream orientation. Flipping them blends diagonals on the wrong side (verified against a diagonal line in XEngineMapDemo: the flipped orientation produces dark fringing along diagonals).
Loaded raw rather than as PNG because forces sRGB + a vertical flip, which would corrupt these data textures - the same reason loads a raw .brdf.

member.summary:
Ensures the instanced rendering VAO and buffer exist for this mesh with enough capacity for instances. Does NOT upload data caller must encode a cmd.UpdateBuffer(instanceBuffer, ...) in the same CommandBuffer as their cmd.DrawIndexedInstanced so the upload is sequenced against the draw.
The instanceBuffer is shared per-mesh across all InstancedMeshRenderables using this mesh. Multiple batches can encode different uploads + draws into one CommandBuffer; the executor processes them in order so each draw sees its own data. If exceeds current capacity, the old buffer is queued for DEFERRED dispose (after frame end) so previously encoded commands holding the old handle still execute against valid GL state.
member.param: Maximum number of instances this call needs to draw.
Output: the instance buffer to upload data into via cmd.UpdateBuffer.
member.returns: The instanced VAO to bind for drawing.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.Resources.SpriteMeshTracer
member.summary: Turns a sprite's alpha silhouette into a tight polygon mesh: it traces the opaque region's outline, simplifies it, and triangulates it. The outline paths are returned alongside the mesh so a future 2D physics collider can reuse the exact same geometry. All coordinates are in pixel space with a bottom-left origin (matching / UV space).

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Resources.SpriteMeshTracer.Generate(System.Byte[],System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Byte,System.Single)
member.summary: Traces + simplifies + triangulates a binary alpha mask. is row-major with a bottom-left origin (length width*height); a texel counts as opaque when its value is >= . is the maximum deviation (in pixels) allowed when collapsing the staircase outline into straight edges; higher = fewer vertices.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.Resources.SpriteMeshTracer.TraceContours(System.Byte[],System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Byte)
member.summary: Extracts the opaque region's boundary as closed loops of grid-corner points. Each unit boundary between an opaque and a transparent (or out-of-bounds) cell becomes an oriented edge with the opaque side on its left; the edges are then stitched into loops. Outer loops wind counter-clockwise.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.VirtualGeometry.Generation.MeshClusterizer
member.summary: Partitions a triangle set into spatially coherent, edge-connected clusters of at most maxTriangles triangles each. Seeds follow Morton order of triangle centroids for global locality, but clusters grow by edge adjacency (flood fill), because raw Morton slicing is discontinuous at Z-order quadrant boundaries and would produce disconnected patches — fatal for the group simplifier, which locks every disconnected border. Import-time tooling — allocation discipline is not required here.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.VirtualGeometry.Generation.MeshSimplifier
member.summary: Quadric error metric (Garland-Heckbert) edge-collapse simplifier for small patches (cluster groups). Boundary vertices are locked in place so sibling groups that share an edge never pull apart, and collapses that flip a face normal are rejected. Errors are accumulated as squared quadric costs and square-rooted once at output. Import time only — allocation discipline is not required here.

member.param: Welded input vertex pool.
Triangle list, 3 pool ids per triangle.
Stop collapsing once at or below this triangle count.
Per-pool-vertex error distances already accumulated by earlier simplification rounds; new collapse costs max into them. Length 0 treated as all-zero.
Squared cost cutoff: candidates beyond it are dropped instead of executed, so the patch under-simplifies rather than baking a huge geometric error. Pass float.MaxValue to disable.
member.summary: Per-call diagnostics (temp: bake investigation).

member.summary: Builds a from a source mesh (Nanite-style whole-mesh cascade): each LOD level simplifies the previous level's entire mesh with QEM (only the mesh's true boundary is locked — no internal group borders, which would fragment the surface into progressively smaller locked patches), then re-clusterizes the result. member.summary: Assigns every fine cluster to the coarse cluster whose bounds best cover it (centroid containment, falling back to nearest bounds center), then reorders the fine clusters so each assignment set is contiguous. Every fine cluster lands in exactly one group, keeping the hierarchy a strict tree.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.ScriptableObject
member.summary: Base class for data assets that live independently of GameObjects (the XEngine equivalent of Unity's ScriptableObject). Subclass this, decorate it with , and create instances via the Assets ▸ Create menu or . Assets are persisted to .asset files in XEngine's Echo text format and resolved at runtime through .

remarks.para: Lifecycle. fires exactly once when an instance becomes resident in the asset cache (on first load via , or immediately when produced by ). fires once when the instance is disposed - either explicitly, or by the asset backend's idle sweep evicting an unreferenced asset. This mirrors Unity's ScriptableObject contract.
Constructing an instance with new does not fire - use for that, which is the path Unity's own ScriptableObject.CreateInstance takes. The distinction matters for assets that do one-time setup in .

Threading. runs synchronously on whichever thread loaded the asset - usually the background thread, not the main thread. Do not touch main-thread-only APIs (rendering, input, GUI) from ; defer that work to or a per-frame system. runs on whichever thread triggered disposal (often the idle-sweep thread).

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Time.FixedAlpha
member.summary: How far the current frame has advanced past the most recent fixed step, as a fraction of in the range [0, 1).
member.remarks:
The leftover of the fixed-step accumulator, published once per frame after the fixed loop and before the update loop. This is the interpolation factor for anything that has to present a simulation running at a different rate than the display — is the one consumer today.
Zero when nothing drives a fixed loop, which is the case in tests that call Scene.FixedUpdate directly. Interpolated bodies then read exactly the last stepped pose, which keeps such tests deterministic.

member.name: T:XEngine.Runtime.MultiValueDictionary`2
member.summary:
A MultiValueDictionary can be viewed as a that allows multiple values for any given unique key. While the MultiValueDictionary API is mostly the same as that of a regular , there is a distinction in that getting the value for a key returns a of values rather than a single value associated with that key. Additionally, there is functionality to allow adding or removing more than a single value at once.
The MultiValueDictionary can also be viewed as a IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey,IReadOnlyCollection<TValue>t> where the is abstracted from the view of the programmer.
For a read-only MultiValueDictionary, see .
member.typeparam: The type of the key.

member.name: M:XEngine.Runtime.RuntimeUtils.ResolveType(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a type from an assembly-qualified name across ALL loaded assembly load contexts, including the collectible context user scripts are loaded into. can only bind names into the default context by CLR rule, so it returns null for any type declared in a user assembly - which is why persisted type names (asset entries, and anything else round-tripped through ) need this instead.
member.remarks: Unlike , this honors the assembly recorded in the name and never falls back to a loose simple-name match, so it cannot return the wrong type when two assemblies declare types that share a name. Assemblies are matched on simple name only: a script assembly keeps its name but gets a fresh version and load context on every hot-reload, so matching full identity would miss it. Returns null rather than throwing for malformed or unloadable names.

member.name: P:XEngine.Runtime.Window.ContentScale
member.summary:
Physical-to-logical pixel ratio for the window's current display.
On Windows, resolves glfwGetWindowContentScale via the native GLFW context to capture the system DPI factor (e.g. 1.25 at 125%). This is needed because FramebufferSize / Size only reflects the ratio when the process is per-monitor DPI-aware; if DPI awareness failed at startup the OS virtualises the framebuffer (fb == win) and the ratio collapses to 1.
On macOS and Linux the GLFW proc address is not reachable via this path, so we fall back to FramebufferSize / Size which is always correct on those platforms (Retina: 3024 fb / 1512 points = 2; 1× monitor: 1).

member.summary: Blends N layers into one output . Layer 0 is the Override base (copied verbatim); each subsequent layer combines per its (Override lerps toward the layer's pose, Additive adds the layer's delta), scaled by the layer weight and a per-bone weight array.

member.name: T:XEngine.Animation.AnimatorControllerRuntime
member.summary: Per-instance evaluator for an . Watches parameters and the current state's normalized time, fires transitions when their conditions (and optional ExitTime) pass, and drives the owning 's mixer layer to activate / crossfade the destination state's clip. The animator owns the actual blending; this type only decides what plays.

remarks.para: Integration. The owning calls once per frame before advancing the playable graph, so any issued here applies in the same frame's graph evaluation. State time for ExitTime checks is read from the current state's clip playable (one frame of lag vs. the just-advanced time, which is imperceptible).
Triggers. A trigger parameter stays set until a transition whose conditions include it fires, at which point it's consumed (reset to 0) — matching Unity Mecanim semantics.

member.name: T:XEngine.Vector.RectTransform
member.summary: A component that stores anchor, pivot, and size information for 2D UI layout. It is a standalone component (not a subclass), required by every UI element; rotation, scale and Z come from the GameObject's regular Transform.

remarks.para: The UI coordinate system is +Y up: anchors, pivots and all grow upward, so increasing AnchoredPosition.Y moves an element toward the top of the screen.

Anchors define how the element's edges attach to its parent rect. Values are normalized (0-1): (0,0) is bottom-left, (1,1) is top-right. When == , the element has a fixed size controlled by . When they differ, the element stretches to fill the anchor range and acts as a padding offset.
Pivot is the local origin of the element (0-1). (0,0) is bottom-left, (1,1) is top-right, (0.5, 0.5) is center.

member.name: T:XEngine.Playables.Clock
member.summary: Time source for a . Owns the global playhead position, a time scale, a wrap mode, and an optional bounded duration. The graph advances the clock each frame via ; scrubbing is performed by setting directly and then calling .
member.remarks:
Two concrete clocks cover the two consumers:
— an unbounded accumulator driven by per-frame deltas. Used by the Animator, where each state advances its own local time and the global clock only provides a stable dt source.
— a bounded, scrubable playhead. Used by the Timeline PlayableDirector, where the global time is the source of truth and every clip's local time is derived from it.

member.name: T:XEngine.Playables.Playable
member.summary: Base class for every node in a . A playable owns a local time, a weight, a playback state, and (optionally) a bounded duration. Subclasses implement the two evaluation hooks and to advance time and produce their typed output.

remarks.para: This is XEngine's equivalent of Unity's Playable / PlayableBehaviour: a general, type-agnostic graph node. Unlike Unity's handle-based model it is a plain class with direct field references — there is no native handle indirection, no port system, and inputs are managed by subclasses via /.

Extensibility: the base class is intentionally public abstract so user code can subclass it (IK jobs, look-at, procedural animation, custom Timeline tracks, ...). Override to advance state, to read child outputs and produce your own. Call base.PrepareFrame(ctx) to keep weight fades running.

remarks.para:
Two time models coexist on purpose:
State-machine driven nodes (e.g. an Animator's clip) read and advance their own local time. They ignore .
Schedule-driven nodes (e.g. a Timeline clip on a track) read and compute their local time from it (localTime = globalTime - clipStart). They ignore for time advancement.

is set when the graph was sampled at a fixed playhead (the caller set the clock time directly rather than advancing it). Schedule-driven nodes use it to skip side effects for times leapt over; state-machine nodes can ignore it.

member.name: T:XEngine.Playables.PlayableGraph
member.summary: A directed acyclic graph of nodes evaluated against a . One graph feeds one or more typed s. Each evaluation runs in two phases — a pre-order pass (advance time/weight, decide which children are active) followed by a post-order pass (read child outputs, produce own output) — then applies every output to its engine target.

remarks.para:
Two entry points cover the two consumers:
— advance the clock by a delta and evaluate. Used by the Animator (continuous, game-time driven) and the Timeline director in play mode.
— evaluate at the clock's current time without advancing it. Used by the Timeline director while scrubbing.

Hot path. and are per-frame and must stay allocation-free. The node walk uses indexed / access (no enumerator), the context is a stack-allocated struct, and the outputs list is a retained field iterated by index. PR0002–PR0007 enforce this.

member.name: T:XEngine.Async.XTaskCompletionSourceCoreShared
member.summary: Shared static state for : the continuation sentinel used to resolve the vs race. The sentinel is never invoked; it is only ever compared by reference.

member.name: T:XEngine.Async.XTaskCompletionSourceCore`1
member.summary:
The shared completion-core logic embedded by value in every single-use XTask source. A struct so it adds no allocation to its host. Implements a single-continuation contract with a version token, a completedCount latch, and deferred auto-reset (the host resets it after so the same instance can be handed back to a new awaiter).
Status is derived on demand from (continuation, completedCount, error) rather than stored, which is one less field to reset and one less race window.

member.name: P:XEngine.Async.XTaskCompletionSourceCore`1.Version
member.summary: Current version token; captured into XTask at construction and validated per call.

member.name: P:XEngine.Async.XTaskCompletionSourceCore`1.IsAwaiterCollectible
member.summary: True while a pending awaiter's continuation or state object belongs to a collectible (hot-reloadable) assembly. Such a source must be dropped from the frame loop when the script AssemblyLoadContext unloads or it pins the whole context. Delegate detection goes through so pooled engine runners instantiated over user state machines are recognized.

member.name: M:XEngine.Async.XTaskCompletionSourceCore`1.Reset
member.summary: Reset the core for reuse: publishes any previously unobserved error, bumps the version (so stale awaiters holding an old token fail fast), and clears all state.

member.name: M:XEngine.Async.XTaskLoopHelper.ClearForReload
member.summary: Hot-reload: drop every pending continuation and polling item that references the collectible script assembly context. Without this, any gameplay coroutine that was suspended at await XTask.Delay/NextFrame/WaitUntil/... pins the whole AssemblyLoadContext and the unload verification fails, forcing an editor restart on every reload.

member.name: T:RequireComponentAttribute
member.summary: Specifies that a GameObject must have certain components in addition to the one where this attribute is applied.
member.remarks:
When this attribute is used on a component, the XEngine Game Engine will automatically add the required components to the GameObject if they are not already present. This ensures that the component has all its dependencies met.
This attribute can only be applied to classes (typically components deriving from MonoBehaviour).

member.param: An array of Type objects representing the required components.
